title: First Term IB Social and Cultural Anthropology Guide
summary: First term IB Social and Cultural Anthropology explained: see likely pacing, reading load, fieldwork, writing tasks, and habits that help you settle in.
body_markdown:
The **first term IB Social and Cultural Anthropology** experience usually begins with a strange discovery: familiar life is much less obvious than it looks.


Your first term will probably combine anthropological vocabulary, ethnographic reading, analytical writing, research methods, ethics, and early observation work. You are not simply learning facts about societies. You are learning to question assumptions, interpret evidence, and compare perspectives without reducing people to stereotypes.


Schools organise the syllabus differently, so no weekly sequence is universal. Most students, however, move through a recognisable arc: learning anthropological language, encountering an ethnography, practising analysis, and discovering how research methods shape what can responsibly be claimed.


### Your first-term overview


By the end of a typical term, expect to have:


- learned concepts such as culture, identity, power, symbolism, social relations, and change
- discussed cultural relativism, reflexivity, positionality, and representation
- read substantial sections of an ethnographic work
- practised using specific evidence in short responses
- explored observation, interviews, ethics, and researcher bias
- completed or planned an early fieldwork-related activity


The[IB Social and Cultural Anthropology resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-social-and-cultural-anthropology) can help you connect these strands instead of treating every lesson as an isolated topic.


### What first-term pacing usually looks like


Concepts, ethnography, methods, and writing tend to overlap rather than appearing in tidy blocks.


Approximate stage What you may study What the work feels like


Weeks 1-3 Culture, perspective, comparison, relativism, reflexivity Discussion-heavy, with unfamiliar terminology


Weeks 4-7 A first ethnography, methods, ethics, positionality More reading and evidence-based paragraphs
